name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,118

clue.text: I adore joiner’s new place in Brazil

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the preceding words are rebuilt in a fresh order

blocks.note: all twelve letters of these three words are used

explanation.surface: A carpenter's latest home turns out to be somewhere in Brazil, and the speaker loves it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rio de Janeiro is a famous coastal city in Brazil, so it is an example of a Brazilian place.

indicators.note: letters that are travelling move about and end up in a new order

blocks.note: both words supply the letters

explanation.surface: Someone from South America hikes up a ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' reads like a direction for the traveller, but its letters are part of the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A Peruvian comes from Peru, a country on the western side of that continent.

blocks.note: first meaning: to attack harshly in words
second meaning: a bid to win all or all but one of the tricks in the card game bridge

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests condemning a deal over a bridge; bridge here is the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: To slam a play is to pan it harshly, and in the card game a grand or small slam is a bid for every trick or all but one.

clue.text: Meagre boxes on floor of vehicle

indicators.note: in a down clue the floor is the bottom, which is the final letter of the word
in a down entry, one piece sitting on another comes above it, so these pieces are read in order

blocks.note: a boxer spars in practice bouts
the final letter of vehicle

explanation.surface: A miserly amount of cargo sits in crates on the floor of a van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' looks like a noun for crates but is the verb meaning fights for practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Something meagre is scanty and thinly provided, which is what sparse means.

clue.text: Some aperitif or sake now abandoned

indicators.note: only some of the letters in the following run of words are taken, as a single unbroken stretch

blocks.note: the run starts at the end of aperitif and stops inside now

explanation.surface: A drink before dinner, perhaps rice wine, now left untouched.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsaken and abandoned are synonyms, both describing something deserted or given up.

indicators.note: the majority is most but not all, so the final letter of the following word is dropped

blocks.note: to long for something is to yearn

explanation.surface: Most of a long twelve-month stretch has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' reads as an adjective about time but is the verb meaning to desire.
explanation.definitionFit: A calendar year consists of twelve months, January through December.

blocks.note: taken as written
to deal is to hand out cards to the players

explanation.surface: A card player dealing a hand exclaims how perfect it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means flawless or exactly as wished, matching perfect.

clue.text: Essential part of diet not ripe unfortunately

indicators.note: something gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the words before it come out jumbled

blocks.note: both words supply the letters

explanation.surface: Fruit that is a key part of someone's diet sadly isn't ripe yet.
explanation.definitionFit: Protein is one of the main nutrients the body needs from food, alongside carbohydrate and fat.

clue.text: Antipodean from north east to stroll around fire

indicators.note: one word is placed around the other, so it splits to hold it inside

blocks.note: N is the compass abbreviation
E is the compass abbreviation
to wander is to stroll aimlessly
fire in the sense of passion or zeal

explanation.surface: Someone from down under walks around a campfire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' reads as a campfire, but it means passion; the antipodes are the lands on the far side of the globe from Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipodean refers to Australia and New Zealand, so a New Zealander is one example.

clue.text: Musician beginning to drink with stranger

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter only

blocks.note: the opening letter of drink
rummer is the comparative of rum, meaning odd or strange

explanation.surface: A band member starts drinking with someone they don't know.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stranger' looks like a noun for an unknown person, but it is the adjective meaning more odd; rum is British slang for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A drummer plays the drums in a band, so is one kind of musician.

indicators.note: sending something back returns it the way it came, so the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: warts are blemishes on the skin

explanation.surface: Hay for livestock is rejected for being blemished.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw is the dried stalks of cereal crops, used on farms as animal feed and bedding.

clue.text: Somehow a jerk with bail can escape?

indicators.note: somehow means by some unknown method, so the letters get put together in an unspecified new way

blocks.note: both words supply letters
joined to the rest by with

explanation.surface: A wonder that some idiot with bail money manages to get away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply adds bail to a jerk to complete the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A jailbreak is a breakout from prison, a particular kind of escape.

clue.text: Heard some low notes in part of tennis court

indicators.note: heard means we go by the sound of the phrase, not its spelling

blocks.note: a bass line is a run of low notes played under a melody

explanation.surface: Deep notes are heard on the tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: On a tennis court the baseline is the back boundary line at each end, behind which players serve.

indicators.note: the odd bits are those in the first, third and fifth positions

blocks.note: letters one, three and five

explanation.surface: Strange scraps of a rude gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is a prompt or signal telling an actor or performer when to begin.

clue.text: Fried potato brother picked up for animal

indicators.note: a sound that is picked up is heard, so the word is taken by how it sounds

blocks.note: a chip is a piece of fried potato
a monk is a brother in a religious order

explanation.surface: A monk lifts a chip to feed a creature.
explanation.walkthrough: A chip is a fried potato stick, the British name for French fries.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipmunk is a small striped rodent of the squirrel family, so it is an animal.

indicators.note: initially points to the starting letter of each of the words before it

blocks.note: the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A sister's racket has upset her grandmother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like an anagram signal, but it only provides its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun is a member of a religious order of women and is addressed as Sister.

clue.text: Flyer that a cutlery shopper may receive?

definitions.text: Flyer that a cutlery shopper may receive?

blocks.clueFragment: Flyer that a cutlery shopper may receive?
blocks.note: surface reading: a leaflet handed to someone buying knives and forks

blocks.clueFragment: Flyer that a cutlery shopper may receive?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a bird whose name is also the invoice for a utensil purchase

explanation.walkthrough: Flyer suggests an advertising leaflet, but it means a bird; the shopper's receipt for a spoon is the bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The spoonbill is a wading bird with a flat spoon-shaped beak, and a flyer is anything that flies.

blocks.note: food gone off is rotten
ice is water in solid form

explanation.surface: A rotten kind of water firm.
explanation.definitionFit: An office can mean a business or firm's premises, or a public department handling affairs.

clue.text: Force the Spanish to follow mischievous creature

indicators.note: one piece follows the other, so it comes second in the answer

blocks.note: an imp is a little devil
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Spanish forces are made to chase a little devil.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in reverse in the clue: the Spanish article comes after the imp.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push someone into action, which is to force them.

blocks.note: first meaning: to call someone over a public address system or ...
second meaning: a boy attendant serving a knight in medieval times

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one instruction to call a knight's helper, but it splits into two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To page someone is to call them by announcement, and a medieval page was a youth training under a knight.

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart, and its pieces can be put back in another order

blocks.note: both words supply the letters

explanation.surface: A paramedic reports that an injured limb is doing fine.
explanation.definitionFit: A fireman fights fires and attends rescues, one of the emergency services workers.

blocks.note: to rid is to free from something
E is the standard abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A European fairground offers a free roller-coaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A roller-coaster is an amusement-park attraction, which is a type of ride.

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, the first and last letters

blocks.note: an organ is a keyboard instrument
the first and last letters of idiosyncratic

explanation.surface: A natural-sounding musical instrument that is wildly quirky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for idiosyncratic but takes only its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic produce is grown without synthetic chemicals, hence natural.

indicators.note: one piece enters the other, going inside it

blocks.note: a Dane is from Denmark
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man named Charlie arrives at a Danish party.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball is a formal social dance event, so a dance is its synonym.
